overall: The AG found a violation only for insufficiently detailed minutes of the January 17, 2012 meeting, ordered them amended and future compliance, and found no violation on notice or executive session; the records-retention question was declined.

allegations.summary: Board's notices for its January 17, 2012 meeting listed abatements generically rather than naming the specific applications to be discussed.
allegations.key_passage: the Board did not violate the law by not listing specific applications to be discussed in the notice for its January 17, 2012 meeting.

allegations.summary: Board reviews abatement applications in closed executive session rather than open session, which the complaint said closes the review to the public.
allegations.key_passage: A board of assessors may enter executive session to discuss and vote on applications for tax abatement or exemption.

allegations.summary: Minutes of the January 17, 2012 meeting lacked a summary of the discussions and a list of documents used.
allegations.key_passage: Here, the minutes do not include a sufficiently detailed summary of the discussion of each abatement application.

allegations.summary: Board does not keep notes, recordings and other materials used to prepare minutes as public records.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore decline to review these allegations, and refer the complainant to the Records Management Unit within the Office of the Secretary of the Commonwealth for any questions about retention of these documents.

allegations.summary: Complaint raised general allegations of wrongdoing by the Board beyond one identified meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Rather, complainants must cite specific allegations of Open Meeting Law violations that occur at identified meetings.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Within thirty (30) days of receiving the determination, amend the minutes of the January 17, 2012 meeting to include a summary of the discussions on each subject.
remedy_passage: We order the Board's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and order the Board, within thirty (30) days of receiving this determination, to amend the minutes of its January 17, 2012 meeting to include a summary of its discussions on each subject.
